title: Prospective non-interventional observational trial in HIV positiv patients with low level viremia under antiretroviral treatment in real life
summary:
In this observational study information of therapy management of HIV-infected patients will be collected and analysed. In about 5% of HIV-patients on correctly taken antiretroviral therapy (ART) a low viral load in the blood can be observed. If this phenomenon is singularly it is called “Blip” (supposed to be known by patients and HIV-physicians), but it can resist as well. 
The purpose of this study is to describe the phenomenon of low viral load under intake of ART in detail. A range of viral load per millilitre (mL) (e.g. 50-400 copies/mL) for this event ought to be defined. A consistent scientific usage should be established talking about the phenomenon of persistent low HI-viral load (LLV). 
Potential correlating factors for LLV should be identified. How does the practitioner react recognizing a LLV? Are there more laboratory tests ordered or is there a change in ART induced? Are these LLV uncritical or a hint for a possible therapy failure? 
In line with the HIV/AIDS quality management agreement of the german Association of Statutory Health Insurance Physicians practitioners specialized in HIV-care document relevant health data quarterly. This documentation is independent of the participation to this survey and takes place regularly. Starting the participation these health data are transmitted pseudo anonymous to the study-centre for further analyses. An amount of 5.000 patients in Germany are supposed to participate for a period of five years.

interventions.name: group with blips (positive HI viral load <401cop/ml and frequency of therapeutic adjustment)
group with low level viremia (at least two positive HI viral loads in a row, range: >50cop/ml - <401cop/ml and the frequency of therapeutic adjustment)
group with detectable HI viral loads >400cop/ml and the frequency of therapeutic adjustment

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients are recruited from the normal patient pool of the participating practises. The following criteria have to be fulfilled:
• the signed informed consent [
• a documented HIV-1 infection
• age ≥18
• on ART treatment (it is also sufficient: - to plan an ART in the next three month after inclusion into the study; - short interruptions of ART due to medical indications or “drug holidays” of max. 90 days, this is not valued as a stopping of ART.
Exclusion criteria:
• participation in clinical trials
• patient not competent to sign informed consent
• missing of sufficient documentation of parameters in the patients records
